channel.title: Hlido — AI agent reviews
channel.description: Independent C2PA-verified reviews of AI agents. Every claim tested, scored on the Laddoo scale, signed with cryptographic provenance.

item.title: Agent Blueprint — Laddoo 64/100
item.description: A cleanly-designed CLI + MCP server that delivers implementation 'blueprints' to coding agents as Agent Skills directories — but the whole thing is gated behind a commercial engagement, so almost nothing about it is independently verifiable.

item.title: tailtest — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: An open-source, hook-based test generator that fires automatically on every AI code edit across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Cline — a genuinely useful answer to 'the AI wrote the code AND the tests, so who actually checked it works?'

item.title: CloudBase AI ToolKit — Laddoo 82/100
item.description: Tencent's official integration layer that wires an unusually broad set of AI coding tools into CloudBase's backend via MCP, Skills and one-click plugins — the widest agent-to-BaaS bridge we've seen, if your backend is (or can become) CloudBase.

item.title: Tool Definition Quality Score (TDQS) — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: An open-sourced six-dimension score for MCP tool descriptions, grounded in two cited studies rather than opinion — reviewed here from its announcement post, which is the only surface that resolved.

item.title: QuokkaPix MCP Runner — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: Lets a cloud AI client drive local image processing without the images ever leaving the machine — and is unusually precise about exactly what the remote control plane does and does not carry.

item.title: crimson-crab — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: A Rust Claude SDK built on one compile-time guarantee — no unwrap, expect, panic! or todo! anywhere in the library — with unknown API surface deserialising into catch-alls instead of breaking builds.

item.title: The Stall — Laddoo 58/100
item.description: An x402 marketplace of agent-callable data services paid in USDC with no accounts — with live usage counters on the page, and almost nothing else Hlido could read.

item.title: Toolport — Laddoo 84/100
item.description: A local MCP gateway that does the two things this layer should do — collapse per-client config and stop tool definitions eating the context window — and it publishes a reproducible benchmark for the second claim.

item.title: ChatSpatial — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: Twenty schema-validated MCP tools over 66 spatial-transcriptomics methods, and it is careful to explain that the tools are the interface and the methods are parameters — a distinction most wrappers blur.

item.title: OpenTakeoff — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: Browser-local construction takeoff that records how every measurement was made — by a person, by one click, or by an agent — which is the right provenance model for a document that ends up in a bid.

item.title: MotionLint — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: Reviews the animation your coding agent cannot see, and splits the job honestly — a deterministic linter for what is measurable, a vision model only for what is not.

item.title: BioMCP — Laddoo 82/100
item.description: One binary and one command grammar over the biomedical databases researchers already trust — unusually well-specified for agent use, and it names its upstream providers instead of hiding them.

item.title: Fal MCP Server — Laddoo 62/100
item.description: A competent MCP wrapper putting fal.ai's image, video and audio models in front of Claude — but it generates synthetic media and says nothing at all about labelling it.

item.title: ProposalCraft — Laddoo 68/100
item.description: An MCP server that drafts client proposals in your own voice, learned from ones that already won — tightly scoped, local-only, and honest that it is a launch-day project.

item.title: Network-AI — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: A governance layer for multi-agent systems that names the real failure mode — agents don't crash, they silently overwrite each other — and discloses its own high-severity CVEs on the front page.

item.title: Anyquery — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: One SQL dialect over 40+ services and every file on disk, exposed to LLMs over MCP — unusually well-executed, with a maintainer-capacity signal published right at the top of the page.

item.title: NeuroLink — Laddoo 60/100
item.description: A broad multi-provider AI streaming layer from an established payments company — undercut by a homepage whose own headline metrics all read zero.

item.title: Gemini CLI — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: Google's terminal coding agent, backed by the strongest distribution in the category — and carrying a prominent replacement notice for free-tier users.
